Survey method.evidence_source: The manuscript states: "While it is necessary to use self-report measures to understand individuals' perceptions and attitudes of the model variables, we relied exclusively on these measures which may have added method variance that increased variable correlations."

Mean BMI of participants.evidence_source: The manuscript states: "Also, we only assessed participants' current BMI." but does not report a numeric mean BMI.

Source of sample.evidence_source: The manuscript states: "Our samples were limited to ... first-year college students..." indicating recruitment from a college sample (first-year students).

Assessment of BA.evidence_source: The manuscript references the Body Dissatisfaction subscale of the EDI-2 and the perceived familial body acceptance subscale of the BAOS, but does not state use of BAS or BAS-2.

Assessment of BMI.evidence_source: The manuscript states both: "we relied exclusively on these [self-report] measures" and "we only assessed participants' current BMI." Combined, these statements indicate BMI was self-reported for Study X.

Correlation between body appreciation an.evidence_source: No correlation coefficients between body appreciation (BAS/BAS-2) and BMI are reported in this limitations section or quoted text.

Number of studies.evidence_source: The text repeatedly refers to "this study" (singular), e.g., "Despite its contributions, this study's limitations need to be addressed." indicating a single study.

section_summary.extract_value: This limitations section notes reliance on self-report measures and retrospective recall, a homogeneous sample of predominantly White, young adult, middle-class first-year college students, and measurement issues (e.g., use of the EDI-2 Body Dissatisfaction subscale and brief subscales of BAOS/PSPS). It calls for future research using multiple informants, more diverse samples, time-specific assessments of caregiver eating messages, validation of the CEMS in clinical populations, and exploration of caregiver characteristics and adaptive eating messages.
section_summary.evidence_source: Key sentences: "While it is necessary to use self-report measures... we relied exclusively on these measures..."; "Our samples were limited to predominantly White, young adult, middle-class, first-year college students..."; "We used the Body Dissatisfaction subscale of the EDI-2..."; and multiple sentences proposing future research directions (e.g., use multiple informants, diverse samples, examine CEMS in clinical populations).
